llm.summary: This is mostly a coherent real-estate skill kit, but its generator and installer have local file-boundary flaws that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: render.py validates the chosen output root but does not sanitize the generated skill name or re-check the final output directory, so a crafted local YAML slug/domain can write SKILL.md and manifest.json outside the intended output tree.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: install.sh persistently copies rendered skills into common agent skill directories under the user's home directory, can overwrite an existing skill directory, and validates the manifest after copying; its manifest entry hashing also trusts a path that can escape the installed skill directory.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill scope is broad and includes sales conversion workflows and adapter-based data lookup, but the inspected instructions are domain-specific and include compliance limits on personal information, financial claims, and unsupported data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent agent-skill installation is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the lack of overwrite controls and the generator path traversal create material risk of unintended persistent agent instruction changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The real-estate calculators, sales SOPs, branded skill templates, and installer match the stated repository purpose, and I found no hidden network exfiltration, destructive commands, or prompt-hijacking instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only run render.py and install.sh on configurations and generated skill directories you trust, inspect generated SKILL.md and manifest.json before installation, avoid rendering untrusted YAML, and verify all tax, loan, and policy outputs against current official sources before using them for real transactions.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed as material: render.py can let configuration-controlled generated names escape the intended output directory, and install.sh can hash a manifest-selected local path outside the copied skill directory.
[TP4] expected: The install and generation flows are disclosed in SKILL.md and README.md, so I do not treat this as hidden tool poisoning; the concern is the unsafe scoping of those disclosed local-write flows.
[P6] expected: The reported 'return rules' snippets return local real-estate rule dictionaries from ruleengine, not system prompts or hidden agent instructions.
[SQP-1] expected: Some trigger text is broad for real-estate workflows, but the inspected instructions stay within real-estate skill selection, calculations, sales SOPs, and branded template generation.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The demo-policy caveat is present, but users could still act on real-estate finance or tax outputs; this is a usage-risk note rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-language defaults are coherent with the stated Chinese real-estate toolkit purpose, and generated templates instruct the agent to use the user's language.
[LP3] expected: The top-level skill does not declare a narrow tool permission set, but inspected behavior is mainly instruction content plus user-run local Python and shell helpers.
